Really enjoyable, but not scary or disturbing. More fun and exciting, oddly enough. For me, it's a lack of restraint, the laundry list of brutalities committed on test subjects just seems unnecessary, at least lacking a build-up. Maybe a part of the log that shows the tests before they discovered the hear weakness? Crazed, sarcophagus-addicted, undead test subjects trying to get back to it until someone accidentally stakes one.

also: "Temporary use of SCP-308 to debrief deceased personnel permitted by Level 4 authorization only." So cool!

item.title: Re-revision wanted
item.content:encoded:
Reading over my handiwork, I have a few comments and one request.
1-I'm not sure what you mean by the clinical tone, soulbane, but I agree that reading the entry leaves something to be desired. Can you be more specific in what areas need work?

2-The entry lacks the horror that I'm sure is there, if only I could express it. I believe it's partially a problem of concept, partially a problem with the way it's presented. As flawed as the original was, it probably did a better job evoking mood than the current version does.

3-The only interesting aspect of the rewrite is similar to many other entries, especially SCP-427.

So my request is: help? Any ideas and criticisms are welcome. If you have big ideas that are hard to explain, feel free to do some edits yourself.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
How exactly does one go about measuring a brain for IQ? It's not a structural thing…IQ can only be measured by active testing. You don't just slap electrodes on it and look at a brainwave monitor.

Even assuming the SCP has access to remarkably high technology (Pretty much a given), such a test would require an advanced brain-machine interface in order to test the cognitive functions.

Hmm….there are several mentions in places about the SCP having apparently relatively commonplace visual and audio implants…but this goes beyond transmitting data to the brain, and into a two-way communication.
